oberflaeche.bereich_untertitel: Guided sessions with a voice. Close your eyes and just listen.
erststart: These meditations are meant to help you relax and unwind. They do not replace medical or psychological advice or treatment.
Do not listen while driving, operating machinery, or in or near water.
You can open your eyes and stop at any time. If strong agitation, distressing images or memories come up: open your eyes, put your feet on the floor, look around, breathe normally.
After lying down, get up slowly.

In a crisis, contact a local crisis line or emergency services. Emergency: 112 (Europe), 999 (UK), 911 (US/Canada). US: call or text 988. Germany: Telefonseelsorge 0800 111 0 111 (free, 24/7). Other countries: findahelpline.com
oberflaeche.erststart_vorsicht: Meditation can also be stressful. If you have trauma-related conditions, experience of psychosis, dissociation, bipolar disorder, severe depression or strong panic: please use these sessions only after talking to your doctor or therapist. Short sessions with your eyes open are the better choice then.
oberflaeche.nebenwirkungen: In studies, about 8% of people report unwanted effects (3.7% in experiments, more in surveys), most often anxiety and low mood. In an 8-week mindfulness course, about 6% had impairments lasting longer than a month – similar to other psychotherapies.

start_blatt.nicht_fahren: Do not listen while driving, operating machinery, or in or near water.
start_blatt.nicht_fahren_einschlafen: Only listen in bed – never while driving. This session is meant to make you sleepy.
start_blatt.offline_fehlt: Please download once with an internet connection. After that, it also works offline.
start_blatt.schlaf_modus_hinweis: No bringing you back and no closing sound: the voice gets quieter and stops.

haltungen.liegen: On your back, a pillow under your head and knees, arms loosely by your sides, legs slightly apart. If you tend to fall asleep and don't want to: bend your knees with your feet on the floor, or sit.
haltungen.sitzen: In a simple cross-legged seat on a cushion, or on a chair with your feet flat on the floor – a chair is just as good. Back upright but not stiff, hands resting loosely on your thighs. If your knees hurt or your legs tingle, change position.
haltungen.im_bett: In bed, in the position you usually fall asleep in; lights off, screen off.
haltungen.augen: Eyes closed or gaze lowered; open is always fine.

zwecke.name: Manage stress
zwecke.ehrlich: Practiced regularly, these exercises can lower stress somewhat; single sessions can calm you in the short term.

zwecke.name: Fall asleep
zwecke.ehrlich: Relaxation is a recognized building block against trouble falling asleep. For long-lasting sleep problems, cognitive behavioral therapy for insomnia is best supported.

zwecke.name: Self-confidence
zwecke.ehrlich: Treating yourself kindly is well studied and can ease self-criticism and pressure. Remembering your own values can give you stability.

zwecke.name: Reach goals
zwecke.ehrlich: The exercise helps you plan a goal (including a work or money goal) concretely, anticipate obstacles and stick with it. Whether money or success follows depends on what you do and on circumstances.

zwecke.name: Deep relaxation lying down
zwecke.ehrlich: Guided relaxation lying down can be deeply calming; if you fall asleep, that's fine.

zwecke.name: Listening
zwecke.ehrlich: Attention practice with sounds; good when the breath as an anchor feels uncomfortable.

zwecke.name: Guided imagery
zwecke.ehrlich: Nature imagery can reduce acute tension and anxiety.

zwecke.name: Recovery for body and mind
zwecke.ehrlich: Relaxation can lower stress, and less stress gives the body better conditions to recover. The exercise cannot heal anything – it complements treatment and does not replace it.

zwecke.name: Short break
zwecke.ehrlich: Three minutes to step out of autopilot.

oberflaeche.offenlegung_stimme: AI-generated voice (neural text-to-speech). Scripts written specifically for this app.
oberflaeche.stopp_hinweis: Tap anywhere to end the session.

atem_stimme.schalter_hinweis: One cue at every change: Breathe in, Hold, Breathe out, Hold empty. That way you can close your eyes.
atem_stimme.bestaetigen_text: This exercise includes breath holds or forceful breathing. Only close your eyes if you are lying down, not in or near water, and not driving.
atem_stimme.bestaetigen_knopf: I'm lying down, not in water, not driving
atem_stimme.leer_erklaerung: “Empty” means holding – with empty lungs, right after breathing out (the pause after the out-breath). It is not a fade-out and not a longer exhale: the exhale is finished, and you wait, relaxed and without pushing, until the time is up.

liste.untertitel: Let the breath come and go. When the mind wanders, kindly come back.
liste.wirkung: Can help reduce stress, anxiety and rumination somewhat – especially with regular practice.
gegenhinweise: With panic or fear of breathing: use sounds instead of the breath as an anchor

wissen.beleg: Mindfulness programs reduced anxiety, depression and pain slightly to moderately (47 studies with active comparison groups), but no more than other active treatments. Meditation apps: small to moderate effect on perceived stress (34 studies).
wissen.ehrlich: Practiced regularly, it can reduce stress and anxiety somewhat.

liste.untertitel: Move your attention slowly through the body, from the feet up to the head.
liste.wirkung: Can help you settle and feel your body more consciously.
gegenhinweise: Trauma: areas can be skipped, eyes open is fine
Severe pain: gently notice the area around it, don't force attention into it

wissen.beleg: As a stand-alone practice, the body scan showed only a small effect on mindfulness and no clear effect on health measures in a meta-analysis (14 papers); studies were small and inconsistent. Better supported as part of the 8-week program.
wissen.ehrlich: Many people find it relaxing; on its own, the effect in studies is small.

liste.untertitel: Briefly tense muscle groups one after another, let go, and notice the difference.
liste.wirkung: Can reduce tension, stress and anxiety, and help you fall asleep.
gegenhinweise: Tense with half your strength, never to the point of pain
Keep breathing while tensing, don't strain or hold your breath (blood pressure)
Leave out injured or recently operated areas and areas prone to cramps
Pregnancy: leave out the belly (practice guideline)

wissen.beleg: Review of 46 papers (over 3,400 adults): less stress, anxiety and depression, but studies varied widely. Sleep medicine (USA, 2021): relaxation methods conditionally recommended for chronic insomnia. Head-to-head comparison: muscle relaxation, breathing and imagery all relaxed people better than doing nothing. In anxious people, it triggered paradoxical anxiety less often than focusing on a word.
wissen.ehrlich: One of the longest-studied relaxation methods; helps many people switch off and fall asleep.

liste.untertitel: Silently repeat short, unchanging phrases and let heaviness and warmth arrive.
liste.start_hinweis: Left-handed? You can start with your left arm in your mind.
liste.wirkung: Can help you relax deeply; works best after a few weeks of practice.
gegenhinweise: Acute psychosis, severe depression: only with professional support
Low blood pressure or dizziness: don't skip the ending, get up slowly

wissen.beleg: Meta-analysis of 60 controlled studies (35 randomized): moderate effects for, among others, tension headache, mild high blood pressure, anxiety, mild depression and sleep problems; mostly older studies. Chronic pain (2021): moderate effect compared with doing nothing, not better than other psychological methods.
wissen.ehrlich: A long-established method; it takes a few weeks of practice before heaviness and warmth come easily.

liste.untertitel: Guided rest between waking and sleep: body rotation, breath counting, opposites, calm images.
liste.wirkung: Can reduce stress and tension and offer deep rest lying down.
gegenhinweise: Trauma, psychosis, dissociation: better not, or only briefly with eyes open
Not a substitute for a night's sleep

wissen.belegstaerke_detail: Stress/anxiety: moderate (large meta-analysis, but low study quality, effects probably overestimated). Sleep: weak (few small studies, inconsistent). “NSDR” as a term of its own: not established.
wissen.beleg: Meta-analysis (2025/26): less stress, anxiety and depression than in comparison groups – clearly so in the studies, but probably overestimated because of their low quality. Only a few small studies on sleep.
wissen.ehrlich: Can relax you deeply and be a break for mind and body.

liste.untertitel: A guided imagery journey to a green meadow, with all your senses.
liste.wirkung: Can reduce acute tension and anxiety; in one study, nature imagery worked better than city imagery.
gegenhinweise: Trauma: not a “safe place” trauma program; eyes open is fine; choose any place you like

wissen.belegstaerke_detail: Individual elements moderate: imagery and nature images reduced tension and anxiety in the short term (a small meta-analysis before surgery, single studies with 48 and 60 people). This exercise itself has not been studied; long-term effects unclear.
wissen.beleg: Imagery before surgery reduced anxiety in a meta-analysis (8 studies); a 10-minute audio with nature images lowered acute anxiety more than the same exercise with city images (48 adults); in a head-to-head comparison, imagery relaxed people both physically and in how they felt. Effects are mainly short-term.
wissen.ehrlich: Calm nature images can help you switch off and feel safer and calmer.

liste.untertitel: In a difficult moment, speak to yourself kindly, the way you would to a good friend.
liste.wirkung: Can help you deal with mistakes and pressure more kindly.
gegenhinweise: Being kind to yourself can at first stir up old pain – go gently, keep it short, stop at any time

wissen.beleg: Meta-analysis (27 randomized studies): less anxiety, depression and stress, more well-being; a newer analysis (56 studies) shows small to moderate effects. The 8-week program was more effective than a waiting list.
wissen.ehrlich: Self-compassion is well studied and can ease pressure and self-criticism.

liste.untertitel: In four steps: wish, best outcome, inner obstacle and an if-then plan.
liste.wirkung: Can help you plan goals more clearly and stick with them. No exercise promises success or money.

wissen.beleg: Meta-analysis (21 papers, about 15,900 people): small to moderate effect on reaching goals, probably somewhat overestimated. If-then plans alone: moderate to large effect in 94 tests; newer corrected estimates are smaller. In experiments, purely positive fantasies of success lowered the energy to act; imagining the process (not just the outcome) helped students more.
wissen.ehrlich: A well-studied planning tool: think about the wish and the obstacle together, and make an if-then plan.

liste.untertitel: Set the day aside, relax the muscles, breathe out slowly. The voice grows quieter and ends without a sound.
liste.wirkung: Can help you switch off and fall asleep more easily.
gegenhinweise: Persistent sleep problems (over 3 months, several nights a week): see a doctor; CBT-I

wissen.belegstaerke_detail: Individual elements moderate: relaxation methods are conditionally recommended for sleep problems, based on weak evidence. This combination itself has not been studied.
wissen.beleg: Relaxation methods are conditionally recommended for chronic insomnia; mindfulness improved sleep quality compared with non-specific comparisons, but not compared with targeted sleep treatments. Best supported is cognitive behavioral therapy for insomnia (CBT-I).
wissen.ehrlich: Relaxation is a recognized building block against trouble falling asleep.

liste.untertitel: Listen to the sounds around you as they come and go, without judging them.
liste.wirkung: Trains attention and is a good anchor when focusing on the breath feels uncomfortable.

wissen.beleg: Hardly studied as a stand-alone practice (one completed study without published results); supported as part of mindfulness programs. “Auditory training” here means attention training with sounds – not better hearing.
wissen.ehrlich: A simple mindfulness practice that also works well when the breath feels unsettling.

liste.untertitel: Three short steps: notice what is here; gather on the breath; widen to the whole body.
liste.wirkung: A short break in everyday life to step out of autopilot.

wissen.belegstaerke_detail: Single practice: weak (no randomized study of its own found). The full 8-week MBCT program: well supported for preventing relapse in recurrent depression.
wissen.beleg: Not tested separately as a single practice. The 8-week program it belongs to lowered the risk of relapse in recurrent depression in 9 studies (38% instead of 49% over 60 weeks).
wissen.ehrlich: A short pause taken from a well-studied mindfulness program.

liste.untertitel: Think of one of your values and of a moment when you acted on it.
liste.wirkung: Can help you stay calmer and more open under pressure.

wissen.beleg: Studied in school, health and conflict settings; effects depend strongly on context and have not been replicated everywhere. Important: reflecting on values is different from statements like “I am wonderful” – in experiments, such statements made people with low self-esteem feel worse.
wissen.ehrlich: Remembering your own values can give you stability before important situations.
